functions.name: ABS
functions.doc: Returns the absolute value of the numeric or interval value.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The numeric or interval value to take the absolute value of. An expression that evaluates to a numeric or interval

functions.name: ACOS
functions.doc: Returns the inverse cosine (a.k.a. arc cosine) of `expr`, as if computed by `java.lang.Math.acos`.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The expression to compute the inverse cosine of. An expression that evaluates to a double

functions.name: ACOSH
functions.doc: Returns inverse hyperbolic cosine of `expr`.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The expression to compute the inverse hyperbolic cosine of. An expression that evaluates to a double

functions.name: ADD_MONTHS
functions.doc: Returns the date that is `num_months` after `start_date`.

params.name: start_date
params.doc: The starting date to add months to. An expression that evaluates to a date

params.name: num_months
params.doc: The number of months to add to the start date. An expression that evaluates to an integer

functions.name: AES_DECRYPT
functions.doc: Returns a decrypted value of `expr` using AES in `mode` with `padding`. Key lengths of 16, 24 and 32 bits are supported. Supported combinations of (`mode`, `padding`) are ('ECB', 'PKCS'), ('GCM', 'NONE') and ('CBC', 'PKCS').

params.name: expr
params.doc: The binary value to decrypt. An expression that evaluates to a binary

params.name: key
params.doc: The passphrase to use to decrypt the data. An expression that evaluates to a binary

params.name: mode
params.doc: Specifies which block cipher mode should be used to decrypt messages. Valid modes: ECB, GCM, CBC. An expression that evaluates to a string

params.name: padding
params.doc: Specifies how to pad messages whose length is not a multiple of the block size. Valid values: PKCS, NONE, DEFAULT. The DEFAULT padding means PKCS for ECB, NONE for GCM and PKCS for CBC. An expression that evaluates to a string

params.name: aad
params.doc: Optional additional authenticated data. Only supported for GCM mode. This can be any free-form input and must be provided for both encryption and decryption. An expression that evaluates to a binary

functions.name: AES_ENCRYPT
functions.doc: Returns an encrypted value of `expr` using AES in given `mode` with the specified `padding`. Key lengths of 16, 24 and 32 bits are supported. Supported combinations of (`mode`, `padding`) are ('ECB', 'PKCS'), ('GCM', 'NONE') and ('CBC', 'PKCS').

params.name: expr
params.doc: The binary value to encrypt. An expression that evaluates to a binary

params.name: key
params.doc: The passphrase to use to encrypt the data. An expression that evaluates to a binary

params.name: mode
params.doc: Specifies which block cipher mode should be used to encrypt messages. Valid modes: ECB, GCM, CBC. An expression that evaluates to a string

params.name: padding
params.doc: Specifies how to pad messages whose length is not a multiple of the block size. Valid values: PKCS, NONE, DEFAULT. The DEFAULT padding means PKCS for ECB, NONE for GCM and PKCS for CBC. An expression that evaluates to a string

params.name: iv
params.doc: Optional initialization vector. Only supported for CBC and GCM modes. Valid values: None or ''. 16-byte array for CBC mode. 12-byte array for GCM mode. An expression that evaluates to a binary

params.name: aad
params.doc: Optional additional authenticated data. Only supported for GCM mode. This can be any free-form input and must be provided for both encryption and decryption. An expression that evaluates to a binary

functions.name: AGGREGATE
functions.doc: Applies a binary operator to an initial state and all elements in the array, and reduces this to a single state. The final state is converted into the final result by applying a finish function.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The input array to reduce. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: start
params.doc: The initial state to start the reduction from. An expression of any type

params.name: merge
params.doc: The binary operator applied to the current state and each array element. A lambda function

params.name: finish
params.doc: The function that converts the final state into the result. A lambda function

functions.name: ANY
functions.doc: Returns true if at least one value of `expr` is true.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The boolean expression to evaluate over the group. An expression that evaluates to a boolean

example.sql: SELECT any(col) FROM VALUES (true), (false), (false) AS tab(col)

functions.name: ANY_VALUE
functions.doc: Returns some value of `expr` for a group of rows. If `isIgnoreNull` is true, returns only non-null values.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The expression to return some value of. An expression of any type

params.name: isIgnoreNull
params.doc: Whether to return only non-null values. An expression that evaluates to a boolean. Must be a constant

example.sql: SELECT any_value(col) FROM VALUES (10), (5), (20) AS tab(col)

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT
functions.doc: Returns the estimated cardinality by HyperLogLog++. `relativeSD` defines the maximum relative standard deviation allowed.

params.name: expr
params.doc: An expression of any type whose distinct values are counted

params.name: relativeSD
params.doc: An optional double literal for the maximum relative standard deviation allowed. Defaults to 0.05

functions.name: APPROX_PERCENTILE
functions.doc: Returns the approximate `percentile` of the numeric, ansi interval or TIME column `col` which is the smallest value in the ordered `col` values (sorted from least to greatest) such that no more than `percentage` of `col` values is less than the value or equal to that value.

params.name: col
params.doc: The numeric, ANSI interval or TIME column whose percentile is computed

params.name: percentage
params.doc: A value (or array of values) between 0.0 and 1.0 specifying the percentile(s) to compute

params.name: accuracy
params.doc: Optional. A positive numeric literal (default: 10000) that controls approximation accuracy at the cost of memory. Higher values yield better accuracy; `1.0/accuracy` is the relative error

example.sql: SELECT approx_percentile(col, array(0.5, 0.4, 0.1), 100) FROM VALUES (0), (1), (2), (10) AS tab(col)

functions.name: APPROX_TOP_K
functions.doc: Returns top k items with their frequency. `k` An optional INTEGER literal greater than 0. If k is not specified, it defaults to 5. `maxItemsTracked` An optional INTEGER literal greater than or equal to k and has upper limit of 1000000.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The expression to compute the top k most frequent items of. An expression that evaluates to a boolean, numeric, date, timestamp, or string

params.name: k
params.doc: The number of top items to return. An expression that evaluates to an integer. Must be a constant

params.name: maxItemsTracked
params.doc: The maximum number of items to track in the sketch. An expression that evaluates to an integer. Must be a constant

example.sql: SELECT approx_top_k(expr) FROM VALUES (0), (0), (1), (1), (2), (3), (4), (4) AS tab(expr)

functions.name: APPROX_TOP_K_ACCUMULATE
functions.doc: Accumulates items into a sketch. `maxItemsTracked` An optional positive INTEGER literal with upper limit of 1000000. If maxItemsTracked is not specified, it defaults to 10000.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The expression whose values are accumulated into the sketch. An expression that evaluates to a boolean, numeric, date, timestamp, or string

params.name: maxItemsTracked
params.doc: The maximum number of items to track in the sketch. An expression that evaluates to an integer. Must be a constant

functions.name: APPROX_TOP_K_COMBINE
functions.doc: Combines multiple sketches into a single sketch. `maxItemsTracked` An optional positive INTEGER literal with upper limit of 1000000. If maxItemsTracked is specified, it will be set for the combined sketch.

params.name: state
params.doc: The sketch state to combine, as produced by approx_top_k_accumulate. An expression that evaluates to the sketch state struct

params.name: maxItemsTracked
params.doc: Optional. The maximum number of items to track in the combined sketch, with an upper limit of 1000000. An expression that evaluates to an integer. Must be a constant

example.sql: SELECT approx_top_k_estimate(approx_top_k_combine(sketch, 10000), 5) FROM (SELECT approx_top_k_accumulate(expr) AS sketch FROM VALUES (0), (0), (1), (1) AS tab(expr) UNION ALL SELECT approx_top_k_accumulate(expr) AS sketch FROM VALUES (2), (3), (4), (4) AS tab(expr))

functions.name: APPROX_TOP_K_ESTIMATE
functions.doc: Returns top k items with their frequency. `k` An optional INTEGER literal greater than 0. If k is not specified, it defaults to 5.

params.name: state
params.doc: The sketch state produced by `approx_top_k_accumulate` or `approx_top_k_combine`

params.name: k
params.doc: Optional. A constant INTEGER literal greater than 0 giving the number of top items to return. If omitted, it defaults to 5

functions.name: ARRAY

params.name: expr

functions.doc: Returns true if a1 contains at least a non-null element present also in a2. If the arrays have no common element and they are both non-empty and either of them contains a null element null is returned, false otherwise.

params.name: a1
params.doc: The first array to compare. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: a2
params.doc: The second array to compare. An expression that evaluates to an array

functions.name: ARRAYS_ZIP

params.name: a1
params.doc: The first array to merge. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: a2
params.doc: The second array to merge. An expression that evaluates to an array

functions.name: ARRAY_AGG
functions.doc: Collects and returns a list of non-unique elements.

params.name: expr
params.doc: An expression of any type whose values are collected into a list

example.sql: SELECT array_agg(col) FROM VALUES (1), (2), (1) AS tab(col)

functions.name: ARRAY_APPEND
functions.doc: Add the element at the end of the array passed as first argument. Type of element should be similar to type of the elements of the array. Null element is also appended into the array. But if the array passed, is NULL output is NULL

params.name: array
params.doc: The array to append the element to. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: element
params.doc: The element to add at the end of the array. An expression of the same type as the array elements

functions.name: ARRAY_COMPACT
functions.doc: Removes null values from the array.

params.name: array
params.doc: The array to remove null values from. An expression that evaluates to an array

functions.name: ARRAY_CONTAINS
functions.doc: Returns true if the array contains the value, false if not. Returns null if the array or value is null, or if the value is not found and the array contains a null element.

params.name: array
params.doc: The array to search. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to check for membership in the array. An expression of the same type as the array elements

functions.name: ARRAY_DISTINCT
functions.doc: Removes duplicate values from the array.

params.name: array
params.doc: The array to remove duplicate values from. An expression that evaluates to an array

functions.name: ARRAY_EXCEPT
functions.doc: Returns an array of the elements in array1 but not in array2, without duplicates.

params.name: array1
params.doc: The array to take elements from. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: array2
params.doc: The array of elements to exclude. An expression that evaluates to an array

functions.name: ARRAY_INSERT
functions.doc: Places val into index pos of array x. Array indices start at 1. The maximum negative index is -1 for which the function inserts new element after the current last element. Index above array size appends the array, or prepends the array if index is negative, with 'null' elements.

params.name: x
params.doc: The array to insert the value into. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: pos
params.doc: The 1-based index at which to insert the value. An expression that evaluates to an integer

params.name: val
params.doc: The value to insert into the array. An expression of the same type as the array elements

functions.name: ARRAY_INTERSECT
functions.doc: Returns an array of the elements in the intersection of array1 and array2, without duplicates.

params.name: array1
params.doc: The first array to intersect. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: array2
params.doc: The second array to intersect. An expression that evaluates to an array

functions.name: ARRAY_JOIN
functions.doc: Concatenates the elements of the given array using the delimiter and an optional string to replace nulls. If no value is set for nullReplacement, any null value is filtered.

params.name: array
params.doc: The array whose elements are concatenated. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: delimiter
params.doc: The delimiter placed between concatenated elements. An expression that evaluates to a string

params.name: nullReplacement
params.doc: The string used to replace null elements. An expression that evaluates to a string

functions.name: ARRAY_MAX
functions.doc: Returns the maximum value in the array. NaN is greater than any non-NaN elements for double/float type. NULL elements are skipped.

params.name: array
params.doc: The array to find the maximum value of. An expression that evaluates to an array

functions.name: ARRAY_MIN
functions.doc: Returns the minimum value in the array. NaN is greater than any non-NaN elements for double/float type. NULL elements are skipped.

params.name: array
params.doc: The array to find the minimum value of. An expression that evaluates to an array

functions.name: ARRAY_POSITION
functions.doc: Returns the (1-based) index of the first matching element of the array as long, or 0 if no match is found.

params.name: array
params.doc: The array to search within. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: element
params.doc: The element to find the position of. An expression of the same type as the array elements

functions.name: ARRAY_PREPEND
functions.doc: Add the element at the beginning of the array passed as first argument. Type of element should be the same as the type of the elements of the array. Null element is also prepended to the array. But if the array passed is NULL output is NULL

params.name: array
params.doc: The array to prepend the element to. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: element
params.doc: The element to add at the beginning of the array. An expression of the same type as the array elements

functions.name: ARRAY_REMOVE
functions.doc: Remove all elements that equal to element from array.

params.name: array
params.doc: The array to remove elements from. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: element
params.doc: The element to remove from the array. An expression of the same type as the array elements

functions.name: ARRAY_REPEAT
functions.doc: Returns the array containing element count times.

params.name: element
params.doc: The element to repeat. An expression of any type

params.name: count
params.doc: The number of times to repeat the element. An expression that evaluates to an integer

functions.name: ARRAY_SIZE
functions.doc: Returns the size of an array. The function returns null for null input.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The array to return the size of. An expression that evaluates to an array

functions.name: ARRAY_SORT
functions.doc: Sorts the input array. If func is omitted, sort in ascending order. The elements of the input array must be orderable. NaN is greater than any non-NaN elements for double/float type. Null elements will be placed at the end of the returned array.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The input array to sort. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: func
params.doc: The comparator function used to determine the sort order. A lambda function returning an integer

example.sql: array_sort(array(5, 6, 1), (left, right) -> case when left < right then -1 when left > right then 1 else 0 end)

functions.name: ARRAY_UNION

params.name: array1
params.doc: The first array to union. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: array2
params.doc: The second array to union. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: str

params.name: expr
params.doc: The expression to compute the inverse hyperbolic sine of. An expression that evaluates to a double

functions.name: BIT_XOR

functions.doc: Merges the two given arrays, element-wise, into a single array using function. If one array is shorter, nulls are appended at the end to match the length of the longer array, before applying function.

params.name: left
params.doc: The first array to merge. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: right
params.doc: The second array to merge. An expression that evaluates to an array

params.name: func
params.doc: The function applied element-wise to merge the arrays. A lambda function
